themes.label: Fed Regime Change — Hiking Leg Paused; Bear-Steepening Structural, Term-Premium Dominant
themes.stance: Prior 'hike pause' framing now updated: effective fed funds stepped to 3.88% in late September (~25bp move), and the 2Y is drifting lower (4.92%→4.75%), meaning the front end is pricing roughly one more hike — not cuts, not a clean pause. Steepener kept but not added to: 10Y at 5.22% (off the 5.31% cycle high), 10Y–2Y stalled at 0.44–0.51 as both ends rallied together last week. FOMC date now uncertain — schedule in hand shows Nov 4–5, not Oct 28 as previously cited; confirm before positioning.
themes.tell: Oct 14 core CPI ≥0.3% MoM + 2Y back above 4.9% = hike risk returns, press underweights. Sub-0.2% core + 2Y break below 4.50% = cut debate opens, cover housing/REIT UW. Nov 4–5 FOMC balance-sheet/QT language = supply-side signal for long end.

themes.label: Core Inflation Trajectory — Services Sticky; Stagflationary Box Risk Rising
themes.stance: Stagflation box intact and the Oct 14 headline print is mechanically set to run hot: September gasoline averaged ~$4.36 vs ~$4.06 in August (~7% MoM), a direct mechanical lift to headline. Base case: core ~0.3% MoM, consistent with Aug +0.29% and July +0.22%. 3-month annualized core ~2.0% is flattered by June's –0.02%; 9-month rate ~2.7%; core PCE since November ~3.2% annualized. October gasoline already rolling over ($4.35 on Oct 5), so September is likely the headline peak. 10Y breakeven slipped to 2.33% despite ~3.7% annualized headline since November — front-end TIPS flagged as underpriced into the Oct 14 print.
themes.tell: Oct 14 core CPI ≥0.3% MoM = full stagflation box confirmed. Two consecutive sub-0.2% MoM core prints = thesis inflects lower. Oct 30 PCE cross-check on whether core PCE continues to run hotter than core CPI; also the reassessment point for front-end TIPS trade.

themes.label: Term Premium / Fiscal Supply Rout — Structural, Independent of Cycle
themes.stance: Intact. 10Y at 5.22% (off 5.31% cycle high); 10Y TIPS ~2.9%; breakevens flat ~2.35% — the long end is overwhelmingly real yield and term premium, not inflation fear. Both ends rallied together last week, leaving 10Y–2Y stalled at 0.44–0.51. Full-Dem Congress base case (90.5% House, 63.5% Senate) = fiscal brinkmanship from Jan 2027, structurally supportive of term premium. Memo cautions: avoid ZROZ until early-Nov Treasury refunding clears.
themes.tell: 10Y sustaining >5.3% on soft Oct 14 CPI = term premium dominant. Early-Nov Treasury quarterly refunding: tailing 30Y auction (clears at higher-than-expected yield) = supply-side confirmation. Strong 30Y auction (tail <0bp) or credible US fiscal consolidation = first real challenge. 10Y–2Y breaking back below 0.25 = regime challenged.

themes.label: Equity–Rate Reconciliation — Record Highs vs. 5.2% Long End; ERP Compressed
themes.stance: Tension persists: S&P futures higher and bull market turns four ('$40T up') even as high-yield spreads widened from 2.93% to 3.15% in two weeks, NFCI tightened six consecutive weeks (–0.551→–0.494), and the broad dollar is up 1.7% since Sep 21. Memo identifies stocks as the outlier, not the signal. M2 growth of ~6% annualized has cushioned equities but is not unlimited. Credit protection flagged as cheap at 3.1% spreads. Big-bank Q3 earnings this week are the first near-term read (date unconfirmed on desk calendar); Oct 14 CPI and Oct 29 GDP are the confirmed macro adjudicators.
themes.tell: HY spreads above 3.5% before Oct 29 GDP = tightening reaching equities, de-risk beta. Big-bank earnings: NIM expansion + benign charge-offs = bull case holds. Margin warnings at mega-cap tech Oct 22–30 = ERP snap risk highest. Spreads back below 3.0% = tightening theme killed.

themes.label: AI Trade Bifurcating — Monetization Crack Arriving Early; Moats vs. Buildout
themes.stance: Crack thesis intact; new evidence: Amazon in talks to acquire AI startup Decart for ~$7B (WSJ) — fits the barbell thesis of cash-rich consolidators buying capability rather than building it (AMZN, MSFT). Rising HY spreads (2.93%→3.15%) hit buildout/financing-dependent names (IREN, data-center plays) first. Memo adds: Oct 29 GDP equipment and software investment line is the first hard read on AI capex durability. Prior stack (OpenAI ~$20B revenue shortfall, Firmus IPO pulled, Broadcom-Anthropic circular financing, Oracle force-majeure) unchanged.
themes.tell: MSFT/AMZN mega-cap earnings (window approx Oct 22–30): capex raised + gross margins intact = moats hold, maintain barbell. Margin warnings or capex cuts = AI de-rating confirmed. Oct 29 GDP capex line stalling = buildout de-rate confirmed. NVDA guide-down or AI credit spreads widening = cohort de-rating.

themes.label: Gulf Escalation / Oil Impulse — Houthis Strike Saudi Core; Supply Still Absorbing
themes.stance: Escalation broadened materially: Houthis struck Riyadh airport twice (13 dead in first strike), extending the Iran-proxy war directly into Saudi Arabia's core. Oil rose on the strikes but still oscillates ~$96 WTI — supply glut continues absorbing geopolitical headlines. Hurricane Isaias trigger missed: storm hit Florida and Alabama, not the Texas/Louisiana refining core, so refiner crack-spread thesis is closed. Memo directs exiting refiners (VLO/PSX/MPC) and holding a light upstream sleeve. Diesel deal (Russian purchase) faces bipartisan pushback and the Ukraine 'energy ceasefire' is already reported violated — may cap crack spreads if it holds, but contested.
themes.tell: WTI sustained above $100 on confirmed Saudi energy infrastructure hit or Hormuz closure = re-press energy and inflation impulse. WTI sustained below $90 with confirmed de-escalation = trim to structural sleeve. OPEC+ late-Nov meeting = next supply lever. Diesel deal collapse/Republican block = refiner crack upside reopens.

themes.label: Arsenal Depletion — Multi-Year Defense Restocking, Multi-Theatre and Broadening
themes.stance: Intact and broadening: Houthi strikes on Riyadh airport raise direct Gulf demand for interceptors (Patriot, THAAD), adding to prior Ukraine/Houthi/Red Sea complex. Transatlantic rift (diesel deal + UK PM Burnham on Russian Brexit interference) supports European self-funded defense spending as an additional demand layer. Full-Dem Congress base case makes defense appropriations a bipartisan floor from Jan 2027. OW XAR, LMT, RTX, NOC.
themes.tell: Prime contractor (LMT, RTX, NOC) earnings order-book guidance raised = demand confirmed, add. Defense supplemental vote in Oct = near-term funding signal. Binding simultaneous ceasefire across Ukraine, Iran/Hormuz, AND Red Sea/Saudi = trim acute premium; multi-year thesis survives on global broadening.

themes.label: Consumer Squeeze — Stagflationary Pressure Reasserting; Real Retail the Deciding Tell
themes.stance: No new evidence today. Prior read unchanged: Aug retail +1.13% MoM nominal (~+0.7% real) is a second data point against the thesis; memo reinforces that the squeeze thesis is fading but not buried. Memo directs covering discretionary shorts. Homebuilder UW remains independently valid on 10Y >5.2% / 2.9% real yields. A third consecutive real-positive September retail print (~Oct 16) would resolve the theme.
themes.tell: Sept retail (~Oct 16): third consecutive real-positive = resolve squeeze thesis, cover remaining discretionary UW. Real-negative reversal = squeeze reasserts, deepen UW. Oct 27 Conference Board Consumer Confidence cross-check.
